transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to convene our cross-office review for the reinstatement case we have before us. As I understand it, the student has applied for reinstatement after a medical leave, and the draft plan currently lists 12 credits for the fall term, places STAT-210 in a regular daytime section, and contains no disability-accommodation or financial-aid conditions. Before I make my binding decision on this plan, I want to make sure we've covered all the necessary bases across offices. Could each of you share any relevant information or concerns from your area that I should be aware of?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical discrepancy. In my advising meeting with the student this week, I confirmed that the student's continuing employment schedule permits a maximum of exactly 9 credits in the fall term. I recorded this in my advising notes, but the reinstatement draft still shows 12 credits. This means the draft plan as written would not be feasible for the student and needs to be revised downward to 9 credits before any decision is made.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical scheduling issue with STAT-210. I confirmed in the registrar's course inventory that the student's required STAT-210 section is offered only online in the summer term, not in a regular daytime section in the fall. The draft plan currently places STAT-210 in a fall daytime section, which is not available. The plan must move STAT-210 out of the fall daytime schedule and identify the online summer section instead. I should note that this inventory update has not yet reached the reinstatement file, which is likely why the draft still shows the incorrect placement.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical disability-accommodation issue. My completed disability-services review confirms that this student has an active accommodation requiring 1.5-times testing time and a reduced-distraction testing setting. This accommodation record has not yet been attached to the reinstatement draft, which is why the draft currently contains no disability-accommodation conditions. The final written plan must include these accommodation conditions before any binding decision is made, as the student is entitled to receive a written plan showing all conditions attached to reinstatement.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical financial-aid condition that is missing from the draft plan. I have confirmed that reinstated financial-aid eligibility requires the student to sign an academic-progress contract by exactly August 15. The financial-aid system has not yet added this condition to the draft plan, which is why it currently contains no financial-aid conditions. This deadline must be included in the final written plan before any binding decision is made, as the student is entitled to receive a written plan showing all conditions attached to reinstatement.
